newsitem.title: USA: Storms batter north Texas, wreck dozens of homes.
newsitem.headline: Storms batter north Texas, wreck dozens of homes.

text.p: Powerful thunderstorms ripped through north Texas on Monday, wrecking dozens of homes, toppling trees and forcing the cancellation of many flights in and out of Dallas.

About 200 people were left homeless when a severe storm with gusting winds of about 80 mph (120 kph) tore into a low-rent apartment complex in south Dallas. It stripped roofs from dozens of apartments, throwing them and air conditioning units onto parked cars and into the streets.
Seven people, including two babies, were hurt by flying debris and one man broke his leg, but there were no serious injuries.
Some local residents said a tornado briefly emerged from the storm and battered the neighborhood, forcing them and construction workers to dive for cover.

"We lost everything. It's all ruined," said Kimberly Jones, whose family joined dozens of others at temporary shelters set up by emergency services after their apartment was seriously damaged by wind and rain.
Elsewhere, many north Texas counties were put on a tornado warning but rescue services said there were no reports of deaths or serious casualties

American Airlines had to cancel almost 300 flights, or about 30 percent of its daily schedule, in and out of Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport and other American flights from here ran up to four hours late. "It has not been a good operating day," airline spokesman Tim Smith said.
Other airlines operating out of Dallas-Fort Worth were also forced to cancel flights as delays mounted, but the situation was better at Dallas' smaller Love Field airport.
The storms dumped 4 inches (10 cm) of rain in some areas and flash floods caused traffic chaos in Dallas, Fort Worth and neighboring towns.
Police reported more than 300 weather-related car accidents in Dallas alone, and further damage to vehicles and homes was caused by pounding, baseball-sized hail across the so-called metroplex.
"I was driving a pretty good sized truck but that wind just blew it straight sideways," said Chuck Dingler.
Meteorological experts said several waves of storms were sweeping through north Texas and would move into southern Arkansas later on Monday.

They said a cold front moving down from Canada and a strong upper-level system in New Mexico was to blame for the bad weather causing heavy storms in the front's warm sector and about 2 inches (5 cm) of snow to fall on much of the Texas and Oklahoma Panhandles.
Electric company officials said about 23,000 homes in and around Dallas suffered power cuts and repair crews were out restoring lines.
Six private planes were badly damaged at the small Spinks Airport near Fort Worth when swirling winds tore the hangar apart.
